UNOFFICIAL 1745-3 whichever is greater, following the receipt of the application and the death confirmation document. (3) Processed and eligibility determined immediately if immediate cremation has been ordered by the medical examiner or coroner. [Eff 08/01/94; am 10/26/01; am 8/19/11 ] (Auth: HRS §346-15) (Imp: HRS §346-15)

§17-1745-5 Determination of eligibility. (a) Deceased medical or financial assistance recipients shall be eligible for the death payments program if: (1) The deceased, at the time of death, is ineligible for the Social Security Administration’s one-time lump-sum death benefit; and (2) A certified death certificate or death confirmation, from agencies with authority to confirm the death, acceptable to the department is received within sixty calendar days from the date of death. (b) The provisions of subsection (a) shall not apply to unclaimed bodies. (c) Eligibility shall be denied if full funeral benefits are available to the deceased from other sources including, but not limited to, pre-paid funeral or burial plans, insurance plans, associations, and clubs. [Eff 08/01/94; am 10/26/01; am 08/19/11 ] (Auth: HRS §346-15) (Imp: HRS §346-15)

body: 1746-2 §17-1746-1 SUBCHAPTER 1 GENERAL PROVISIONS §17-1746-1 Purpose. The purpose of this chapter is to describe the PACE Hawaii Program, eligibility requirements, and services provided under the PACE Hawaii Program. [Eff 01/29/96 ] (Auth: SLH 1992, Act 211; HRS §346-59) (Imp: HRS §346-14; 42 C.F.R. §434.20) §17-1746-2 Definitions. For the purpose of this chapter: "Capitation payment" means the negotiated prepaid fixed dollar amount the department pays each month on behalf of each PACE enrollee to PACE whether or not the PACE enrollee receives services during the month covered by the payment. "Medicaid reimbursement" means the payment made to Medicaid providers for Medicaid services rendered to eligible recipients. "PACE" means the PACE Hawaii Program which is a demonstration project to provide an array of health related services within a capitation payment. "PACE enrollee" means an individual who voluntarily elects to receive services through the PACE provider. "PACE provider" means the Maluhia Long Term Care Health Center under the state department of health. "Subcontractor" means an organization or individual who has entered into a contract with PACE to provide medical or health related services for PACE participants. [Eff 01/29/96 ] (Auth: SLH 1992, Act 211; HRS §346-59) (Imp: HRS §346-14; 42 C.F.R. §434.20) §17-1746-3 (Reserved) SUBCHAPTER 2 PACE PROVIDER REQUIREMENTS §17-1746-4 PACE provider requirements. (a) A PACE provider that provides all or part of the required PACE services indirectly through a subcontractor shall enter into a written subcontract with the individual or organization. The written subcontract shall stipulate, at the minimum: (1) Name and address of the subcontractor; (2) Service to be provided by the subcontractor; (3) Conditions for payment; (4) Statement of functions and responsibilities of the PACE provider and the subcontractor; and (5) Other items agreed to by the PACE provider and the subcontractor. (b) The PACE provider shall submit the subcontract to the department for approval and commence the subcontract provisions after approval has been obtained from the med-QUEST division. (c) The PACE provider shall be responsible to the department for the provision of all PACE services. No subcontract between the PACE provider and the subcontractor shall terminate the legal responsibility of the PACE provider to the department. (a) An individual who elects PACE shall waive all rights to Medicaid payments for services that are equivalent to PACE services. [Eff 01/29/96 ] (Auth: SLH 1992, Act 211; HRS §346-59; 42 C.F.R. §434.20) (Imp: HRS §346-14; 42 C.F.R. §434.25, 434.26, 434.27) §17-1746-15 Covered services. (a) Services available to PACE enrollees shall be negotiated by the department and the PACE provider. The cost of providing PACE services and the administrative costs for the PACE provider shall be included in the capitation payment. (b) The covered services may be provided by the PACE provider either directly or indirectly through subcontractual arrangements in accordance with the provisions set forth in this chapter. (c) At the minimum, PACE services shall include: (1) Multidisciplinary team to assess, develop, implement and evaluate the treatment plan of each participant enrolled in PACE; (2) Adult day health services of which the core services include health related services, nursing services, maintenance therapies, social work services, recreational therapy, and dietary services;

body: 1746-8 §17-1746-19 (b) The PACE provider shall make any of the PACE records available to the department or its representatives, Department of Health and Human Services, and other authorized federal and state agencies. body:
§17-1747-1

Laws of Hawaii 2022, section 2. The Hawaii child wellness care program provides one payment of $50.00 per year per child as an incentive to Medicaid beneficiary parents for completing an annual well- child examination for each child of that Medicaid beneficiary. [Eff MAR 24 2024 ] (Auth: HRS §346- 14) (Imp: SLH 2022, Act 127, §2)

§17-1747-2 Definitions. As used in this chapter:

"Annual" means once in a twelve-month period.

"Child" means an unmarried individual who is under eighteen years of age. "Child" includes a stepchild and an adopted child.

"Department" means the department of human services of the state of Hawaii, which includes the single state agency responsible for administering the medical assistance program.

"Hawaii child wellness care program" means a $50.00 incentive to Medicaid beneficiary parents for completing an annual well-child examination for each child of that Medicaid beneficiary; provided that only one annual payment be made per child, pursuant to Act 127, SLH 2022.

"Licensed health care professional" means a primary care provider licensed by the State, including a physician, physician assistant, or advanced practice registered nurse.

"Medicaid beneficiary parent" means an individual who is actively enrolled in Medicaid as a beneficiary and is legally responsible to support the child(ren).

"Well-child examination" means a routine examination of a child performed by a licensed health care professional as part of preventive pediatric care that includes a review of the child’s family-centered health history; a physical examination; immunizations; a comprehensive review of systems to include vision and hearing screening; a developmental and behavioral assessment; an oral health risk assessment; a social assessment; parenting education on a range of topics;

$50.00 incentive per child. The $50.00 incentive is limited to a single annual payment, subject to availability of funding, provided the following are met:

(1) Participant eligibility determined by using an application form prescribed by the department;

(2) Completion of a well-child examination as defined in section 17-1747-2; and

(3) The well-child examination is validated by a licensed health care professional.

(bp) Issuance of the $50.00 incentive payment per child shall be provided to the Medicaid beneficiary parent when an individual is determined to be eligible.

(c) Upon a determination of ineligibility for the $50.00 incentive, the applicant shall receive a notice of denial.

(1) The applicant shall be granted a review of

the denial by the department; and

(2) The department’s decision from the review will be final. [Eff WAR 24 ]
